name: Frank Sherwin Bridge
connectingPointsDisplay: St. John's Road — Wolfe Tone Quay
facts: Frank Sherwin Bridge, unveiled in 1982, was engineered to divert heavy traffic from the cramped Sean Heuston Bridge, easing congestion along Dublin's historic quays.

The three‑span reinforced concrete design of Frank Sherwin Bridge marked a modern engineering milestone, replacing older stone arches with robust, low‑profile spans that blend seamlessly into the cityscape.
Named after Dublin politician Frank Sherwin, the bridge’s opening reversed the one‑way system on the quays, establishing north quays eastbound and south quays westbound for the first time.
